<explanation>
1. Project Type & Purpose  
   - This is a monorepo for a full-stack, API-first authentication & user-management platform named “Hanko.”  
   - Core pieces:  
     • A Go-based backend API providing authentication (passkeys, passcodes, passwords), OAuth SSO, SAML SSO, webhooks, sessions, MFA, JWT issuance, user-management, audit logging.  
     • A “Hanko Elements” Web Components library (React/TS) for embedding login/registration/profile UIs.  
     • A “Hanko Frontend SDK” (TS) that encapsulates HTTP flow-API calls and client-side session/event handling.  
     • Example apps (Angular, Next.js, React, Vue, Svelte, Fresh, Express) and a Go “quickstart” demo.  
     • Deployment manifests (Docker Compose, Kubernetes) and end-to-end tests (Playwright).  

2. File Structure Analysis  
   - Top-level directories:  
     • backend/ – Go service with subpackages for config, crypto, DTOs, flow_api, persistence (models + migrations), handlers, middleware, webhooks, CLI commands, and “ee” (enterprise) SAML support.  
     • frontend/elements/ – embeddable UI components packaged as an npm library.  
     • frontend/frontend-sdk/ – TS HTTP & event client for backend API.  
     • frontend/examples/ – starter templates for various frameworks.  
     • quickstart/ – a minimal Go HTTP + static frontend showing integration.  
     • deploy/ – Docker Compose and Kustomize for Kubernetes.  
     • e2e/ – Playwright tests running against a seeded environment (uses MailHog & Postgres).  

3. Key Insights from README  
   - Architecture section calls out three building blocks: backend, elements, frontend-sdk.  
   - It’s API-first and cloud-native.  
   - Deployment examples show Postgres for persistence, MailHog (or SMTP) for email, optional Redis or in-memory for session/rate-limiting.  
   - Supports external OAuth providers and SAML IdPs.  

4. Designing the System Diagram  
   a. Main Components (containers/services):  
      • Browser (client) hosting a consumer app that pulls in Hanko Elements or calls Hanko Frontend SDK.  
      • Hanko Frontend SDK / Elements (JS in browser).  
      • Hanko Backend API (Go HTTP server).  
      • PostgreSQL database.  
      • Mail service (SMTP or MailHog).  
      • Optional Redis (rate limiter, cache).  
      • External identity providers – OAuth providers (Google, GitHub, Apple, etc.), SAML IdP(s).  
      • Webhook targets (external HTTP endpoints).  

   b. Relationships & Data Flows:  
      1. User → Browser → Hanko Elements (or custom UI using Frontend SDK) → HTTP(S) → Hanko Backend API.  
      2. Backend API ↔ PostgreSQL (CRUD on users, passkeys, sessions, flows).  
      3. Backend API → SMTP/MailHog (for verification emails, passcodes).  
      4. Backend API ↔ Redis or in-memory store (for rate-limiting or device-trust cookies).  
      5. Backend API ↔ External OAuth providers (OAuth2 exchanges).  
      6. Backend API ↔ External SAML IdP(s) via SAML flows (enterprise edition).  
      7. Backend API → Webhook targets (on events like user created, login success).  

   c. Architectural Patterns & Design Principles:  
      • Layered architecture in the backend: HTTP handlers → service layer (flow_api, business logic) → persistence layer → migrations/models.  
      • CLI commands use Cobra for ops (migrations, key management, schema export).  
      • API-first approach: all features exposed as REST endpoints, with interactive flow API.  
      • Distributed configuration via YAML and environment variables.  
      • Monorepo containing multiple deployable artifacts (Go binary, npm packages, example apps).  

   d. Key Technologies & Frameworks:  
      • Go modules, Cobra CLI, fizz/migrate for DB migrations  
      • PostgreSQL, optional Redis  
      • SMTP (MailHog) for email  
      • React + Webpack for Hanko Elements  
      • TypeScript for Frontend SDK  
      • Playwright for E2E tests  
      • Docker Compose & Kubernetes (Kustomize) for deployments  

5. Tailoring the Diagram for This Full-Stack Application  
   - Draw separate boxes for:  
     • Frontend (Browser + Elements/SDK)  
     • Backend API (annotate sub-components: Handlers, Flow API, Persistence)  
     • Database (Postgres)  
     • Supporting services (Redis, MailHog)  
     • External systems (OAuth, SAML IdP, Webhook targets)  
   - Emphasize the HTTP boundary between browser and backend, plus any message queues or webhooks.  
   - Show optional overlays: quickstart demo embedding Elements in a Go server; examples as standalone static apps.  
   - Illustrate Docker Compose services vs. Kubernetes pods if desired.  

6. Diagram Best Practices  
   - Label each component clearly (e.g., “hanko-backend:8000”, “Postgres:5432”).  
   - Use directional arrows to show data flow (→).  
   - Color-code:  
     • Blue for frontend/browser components  
     • Green for backend components  
     • Orange for data stores  
     • Gray for external systems  
   - Use consistent shapes:  
     • Cylinders for databases  
     • Clouds for external IdPs/webhooks  
     • Rectangles for services  

Note: Capture all essential building blocks (backend services, DB, cache, mail, external providers, frontend libraries), their interactions, and how the traffic flows end-to-end. This level of detail ensures an accurate, maintainable system design diagram.  
</explanation>
